fix.en: to prepare, arrange; to get (money, home)

ex.en: We're putting together money for the wedding.
We prepared food for the guests.
We finally got a home of our own.

fix.note: 회사원 = office worker; 신입 사원 = new hire.

ex.en: I'm a new employee.

ex.s: 그 회사는 사원이 백 명쯤 돼요.
ex.en: That company has about a hundred employees.
I left my employee ID at home.
Did you save the file?
Please save my number.
I saved the photo to my phone.

fix.note: Usually 시험해 보다 = to try out.

ex.en: I tried out the new feature.
Are you testing me right now?

ex.s: 사기 전에 매장에서 한번 시험해 보세요.
ex.en: Try it out in the store before you buy.

fix.note: 연애하다 = to date, be in a relationship.

ex.en: Are you seeing anyone these days?

ex.s: 두 사람은 오 년 연애하고 결혼했어요.
ex.en: They dated for five years and then got married.
Can you give me some dating advice?
Five hundred grams of pork belly, please.
Put in just 20 grams of sugar.
How many grams does this package weigh?

fix.note: Usually an office building; homes are 아파트 or 집.

ex.en: That tall building is our office.
There's a convenience store on the building's first floor.
There are so many tall buildings in Seoul.
The bag is way too heavy.
The luggage weight limit is 23 kilos.
Let me weigh it.

fix.note: Used before nouns: 임시 비밀번호, 임시 휴업.

ex.en: A temporary password came by text.
This is a place we're staying temporarily.
The store is temporarily closed today.

notes: Fixed one stiff seat-arrangement sentence, an uncommon 사원 식당, a 저장되다 (passive) example, and a duplicate "tried out" example. Dropped 상관 as a duplicate of 상관없다 (ev-15).
